CoverCancellationFailureTests.A_throwing.reason: Source 43's deliberately throwing cancellation callback does not replace cancellation: the actual HTTP caller sees cancellation, the source completes, and a later retry succeeds. At the renderer boundary a rejected cancellation IPC cannot restore the canceled consumer or publish late bytes. Tests verify zero pending/live slots, no stale query data, cleanup and repeated shutdown. React canceled leases resolve null rather than exposing an Avalonia Task cancellation to a view model.

CoverConversionBoundaryTests.A_disk_hit_.reason: The source-exact one-permit SlateBlue 160 x 240 fixture holds source 42 while disk 43 finishes within one second, then releases42. The actual HTTP endpoint also serves cached 43 while all four unrelated network fetches remain held. The renderer separately proves six pending network reads cannot occupy its six browser conversion slots. Backend PNG encoding and browser decoding each have a bounded permit; normal fetching occurs outside it, with the documented bounded encoded-queue overflow reread exception.

CoverConversionBoundaryTests.A_failed_fl.reason: The precise source operation is converting a second Avalonia floor bitmap after the vivid bitmap has already converted. Electron has one decoded image and applies the shared numeric dormancy floor with CSS, so there is no second bitmap conversion or partially converted vivid/floor pair to port. The unchanged original test still passes. The applicable failure-cleanup behavior is independently verified: actual PNG encoder failure disposes its decoded bitmap and returns its permit before retry, and browser conversion failure revokes its URL and retires the queued job.
